result_text:
Any folder whose name starts with `mock` or `__mock` now counts as mock resources, whatever follows in the name. I didn't write or run a check of your example folders, so the new rule is untested. I ran the scoping and convention tests in `codeanalyzer`, and they passed.

I changed two regexes in `ScopingConventions.java` (around line 393). The folder-name part was `[a-zA-Z0-9_\- ]+`, which needs at least one more character after `mock` and only allows those characters. It is now `[^/]*`, so these are covered:
- A plain `mock` folder, and names with punctuation or non-ASCII characters (`mock.data`, `mock(old)`, `mock-größe`, `mock模拟`).
- All the folders that matched before (`mocks`, `__mocks__`, `mock-data`, `mock_data`, `mock data`, `mockStore`).
- Backslash paths, which `SourceFileFilter.pathMatches` already normalises.

The match is still anchored on a `/` just before `mock`, so `remock/`, `demo/`, `src/main/java/`, `mock.java` and `mockery.java` stay out of test code.

I didn't add new test cases.
